name: UGC Creator
description: A natural execution resembling organic content created by a user or creator, built around authenticity, directness, and an everyday product-use context.
rules: The execution should feel authentic and unscripted.
Avoid an overly promotional, corporate, or excessively polished feel.
Communication should be direct, natural, and relatable.
Prioritize realistic situations, people, and environments connected to the audience’s everyday life.
The product should appear naturally in a real-life usage context.
Minor visual imperfections are acceptable if they increase credibility and authenticity.

name: Faceless
description: An execution that does not rely on a visible person addressing the audience directly, but instead uses the product, hands, the user’s point of view, surroundings, interface, graphics, or text.
rules: Do not base the ad on a traditional presenter or talking head.
Build the communication around the product, hands, the user’s point of view, surroundings, graphics, interface, or text.
Every element of the ad should be understandable without showing the presenter’s face.
The product, its functionality, or its outcome should remain a regular focal point.
Maintain a clear visual flow that guides the audience through the message.
Do not show faces merely to fill space—the presence of people should serve a communication purpose.

name: Lifestyle
description: An execution that presents the product as a natural part of the audience’s lifestyle, set within an everyday, aspirational, or relatable context.
rules: Show the product in situations connected to the audience’s real life and needs.
The environment, people, and situations should align with the target audience and the brand’s positioning.
The product does not need to dominate every element, but its role in the story must be clear.
Prioritize natural interactions and usage contexts over isolated product presentations.
Build emotion through the situation, people, environment, and outcome.
Avoid random lifestyle elements that do not support the ad’s main message.

name: Documentary
description: An authentic, observational execution resembling a record of a real experience, story, process, or situation involving the product and its user.
rules: The execution should feel like observing a real situation rather than watching a staged advertisement.
Prioritize realistic people, places, behaviors, and contexts.
Avoid an overly staged, polished, and typically commercial aesthetic.
Show real experiences, processes, reactions, or outcomes.
Minor imperfections are acceptable if they increase the sense of authenticity.
The product should be part of a genuine story rather than an element artificially added to the message.

name: Product Focused
description: An execution in which the product is the main focus of the ad, with its appearance, functionality, features, and usage serving as the most important visual elements.
rules: The product should be one of the most important and visible elements of the ad.
Highlight details, usage, functions, or properties that are relevant to the main message.
Every visual element should help the audience understand the product, how it works, or the value it provides.
Limit elements that distract attention from the product.
Show the product in use when doing so helps explain its benefits.
The product’s visual presentation should support its positioning and perceived value.

name: Studio Commercial
description: A polished, controlled commercial execution featuring high visual quality, precise composition, and a professional presentation of the product or brand.
rules: Use clean, controlled, and intentionally designed compositions.
The execution should look premium, professional, and cohesive.
Every visual element should have a clearly defined purpose.
The product or main message should be presented without unnecessary visual clutter.
Avoid the accidental rawness and unfinished elements associated with organic UGC.
Maintain consistent colors, styling, and composition throughout the ad.

name: Founder Led
description: An execution centered on the brand’s founder, their story, experience, motivation, and personal credibility.
rules: The founder should be the primary source of credibility and narration.
Communication should feel personal and direct.
Emphasize the authentic story behind the creation of the product, brand, or solution.
Show the founder’s real experiences, observations, or motivations.
Avoid a corporate, anonymous, or overly staged tone.
Present the product as a response to a genuine need, problem, or experience encountered by the founder.

name: Graphic Led
description: An execution driven primarily by typography, graphics, icons, diagrams, data, and visual communication of information.
rules: Graphics and typography should be the main carriers of the message.
Text should be concise, legible, and easy to scan.
Every graphic element should serve a specific communication purpose.
Maintain a consistent system of typography, icons, composition, and information hierarchy.
The product or its visual representation should appear at key moments.
Avoid decorative graphic elements that do not help the audience understand the message.

name: Interface First
description: An execution in which the product’s interface, screen, dashboard, website, or digital user experience is the primary means of demonstrating its value.
rules: The product interface should be one of the ad’s main visual elements.
Show specific functions, actions, and outcomes instead of random screens.
Direct the audience’s attention to one clear action, function, or benefit at a time.
The most important interface elements must be easy to notice and understand.
Additional text or graphics should support the audience’s understanding of the product rather than duplicate the interface.
Avoid overwhelming the audience with too many elements, functions, or pieces of information at once.

name: Hybrid
description: A flexible execution combining several presentation styles, such as UGC, lifestyle, product-focused, graphics, interface-based, or more polished commercial content.
rules: Combine different styles only when each serves a specific purpose within the ad.
Maintain consistency in tone, branding, and the main message despite mixing different presentation styles.
Do not change the presentation style without a clear narrative or communication reason.
Use different styles for different purposes, such as authenticity, demonstration, explanation, proof, or product presentation.
Each presentation style should support the structure of the selected ad framework.
Avoid randomly mixing techniques solely to make the ad more dynamic.
